findings.message: CRITICAL: Unsigned process executing from user-writable directory: svchost_update.exe (PID: 5824)
findings.remediation_title: Unsigned Executable in User-Writable Staging Directory
findings.threat_analysis: Malicious implants, infostealers, and secondary stage loaders frequently execute from AppData, Temp, or ProgramData to bypass standard directory ACLs without requiring administrative write privileges.

remediation_steps.action: Terminate the rogue process immediately using its Process ID (PID).
Copy the suspicious binary to an isolated quarantined location for hashing and reverse engineering before deletion.
Permanently remove the unverified binary from the user profile.
Confirm no residual child processes or reinfection routines are executing.

findings.module: 4. Registry Run Keys & Image File Execution Options (IFEO)
findings.message: Suspicious Registry Persistence entry invoking LOLBin or user-writable path: WindowsUpdateChecker
findings.remediation_title: Suspicious Registry Run Key Invoking LOLBin / Encoded Command
findings.threat_analysis: Adversaries maintain userland persistence across reboots by creating registry values in HKLM/HKCU Run keys that trigger living-off-the-land binaries (LOLBins) like powershell.exe, cmd.exe, or mshta.exe with hidden or encoded commands.

remediation_steps.action: Remove the malicious autorun registry property.
Search for any active processes spawned by the autorun script.
remediation_steps.command: Get-CimInstance Win32_Process | Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -like "*WindowsUpdateChecker*" } | Select-Object ProcessId, CommandLine

remediation_steps.action: Ensure the registry value has been completely eradicated.

findings.module: 5. Non-Standard Services & Unsigned Running Kernel Drivers
findings.message: Third-party service running outside standard Windows system32: CustomTelemetrySvc
findings.threat_analysis: Third-party services executing outside Windows System32 can be leveraged for defense evasion or unauthorized persistence. Inspect the binary path, vendor digital signature, and startup arguments.

remediation_steps.action: Query the service configuration and verify vendor signature.
Halt the service and prevent automatic startup.
Delete the service entry if confirmed malicious.
